landing.title: You can see who opened your medical record
landing.lead: ShifoSafe is an electronic medical record for a clinic. A doctor opens your record only for the period you allowed, and every access shows up in your account with a name and a time.
landing.shotAccessAlt: The Access history page in the patient account: accesses by a doctor, a lab technician and an administrator, with date and time
landing.shotAccessCaption: The Access history page in the patient account (Uzbek interface). Names and records are samples, not real patients.
landing.consentTitle: You give permission, and you take it back
landing.consentP1: You pick a doctor and a period: 1 day, 7 days, 30 days or no end date. You can revoke the permission at any time. The doctor you are booked with today can see your record until the end of the day.
landing.consentP2: In an emergency a doctor can get in without permission, but must write down the reason. That access closes by itself after 60 minutes, the security team is notified, and it is shown to you.
landing.shotConsentAlt: The Permissions page: choosing a doctor, a period, and a button to revoke a permission
landing.shotConsentCaption: The Permissions page with sample data (Uzbek interface).

patient.title: Patient
patient.a: Books a visit to a doctor online.
patient.b: Reads their medical history, prescriptions and lab results, and downloads the history as a PDF.
patient.c: Gives a doctor permission and watches who opened the record.

doctor.title: Doctor
doctor.a: Sees today's queue and calls the next patient.
doctor.b: Writes visit notes and prescriptions and attaches files.
doctor.c: Opens only the records of patients who gave permission or are booked for today.

desk.title: Front desk and laboratory
desk.a: Registers a patient and adds a 3×4 photo to the record.
desk.b: Issues a queue ticket, and a temporary password for a patient who forgot theirs.
desk.c: A lab technician enters the result, and the patient sees it in their account.

landing.checksLead: The word “secure” proves nothing by itself. So we list what was done, with dates.
landing.checksOpen: The test suite and the results are published openly:

pentest.what: An independent tester attacked the system from outside and reported 9 findings. The confirmed ones were fixed.

retest.what: A re-test on the running system passed 89 of 89 tests.

restore.what: A backup was restored into a separate database and verified. Backups are taken every 6 hours and kept encrypted in three places.

ci.what: More than 360 automated tests run, and the libraries in use are checked for known vulnerabilities.

landing.aboutP1: ShifoSafe was built at the Department of Software Engineering of Andijan State University as part of a master's thesis in information security. Author: Alisher Voitov.
landing.aboutP2: It is a research prototype. The system works and has been checked, but it is not yet officially in use at any clinic.
landing.footerNote: A research prototype built for a master's thesis

alerts.title: Security alerts
alerts.lead: The system watches the audit log and flags suspicious staff activity. An alert is not always a breach: check the situation and mark it as reviewed.

response.logout: All sessions were automatically closed (must sign in again).
response.lockedDone: The account was suspended — restored after review.

alerts.note: Thresholds are set in the server settings (SECURITY_ALERTS). Every alert is also written to security.log.

sessions.lead: Devices currently signed in to your account. If you see one you don't recognise, sign it out and change your password.

sessions.confirmOthers: Sign out every device except this one?
sessions.confirmAll: You'll be signed out everywhere, including this device. Continue?
sessions.relogin: To mark this device in the list, sign out and sign in again once.
sessions.note: A signed-out device is disconnected within seconds and needs the password to sign in again. Device names are estimated from browser data.
sessions.actionError: Couldn't complete the action. Please try again.

integrity.ok: Chain intact: none of the {{count}} entries has been altered or deleted.
integrity.okHint: Every entry's hash was recomputed and its link to the previous entry checked.
integrity.bad: Warning! The audit log has been tampered with: {{count}} problem(s) found.

type.link: preceding entries were deleted or reordered
type.truncated: entries were removed from the end (checkpoint mismatch)

integrity.head: Head hash
integrity.note: Each entry stores the hash of the previous one (HMAC-SHA256 chain). Altering or deleting even one entry in the database breaks the chain. The system verifies it nightly and raises a security alert on any break.

qstats.note: Wait: from arrival at the clinic until called. No-show rate: no-shows / (seen + no-shows); cancelled and open tickets are excluded.

mfa.title: Two-step sign-in
mfa.lead: Even if your password is stolen, nobody can sign in: a 6-digit code from the Google Authenticator app on your phone is also required.
mfa.forced: Two-step sign-in is mandatory for administrator and doctor accounts. Other sections stay locked until you set it up.
mfa.usedBackup: You signed in with a backup code. {{n}} backup codes left — create new ones if you are running low.
mfa.step1Text: Install Google Authenticator (or Microsoft Authenticator) from Google Play / App Store.
mfa.step2Text: In the app tap “+” → “Scan a QR code”.
mfa.step3Text: Enter the 6-digit code shown in the app.
mfa.manualKey: Can't scan? Enter this key manually:
mfa.regenHint: Enter the current code from the app. Old backup codes will stop working.
mfa.disableText: If you turn off two-step sign-in, your account is protected by the password only.
mfa.resetConfirm: Reset two-step sign-in for {{name}}? They will be signed out of all devices and set it up again on next sign-in.
mfa.note: Lost your phone? Sign in with a backup code and set up 2FA on the new phone. If the codes are lost too, contact an administrator.

kiosks.title: Kiosk keys
kiosks.lead: Each kiosk screen in the hospital works with its own secret key. If a key is lost or a device is replaced, revoke only that kiosk — the others keep working.
kiosks.step1: On the kiosk device, open the site's /kiosk page.
kiosks.step2: Enter this key in the “Kiosk setup” window.
kiosks.shownOnce: The key is shown only now. Do not send it by messenger or email — type it directly on the kiosk device.
kiosks.legacy: The shared key from the server settings (QUEUE_KIOSK_KEY) is still active. Once all kiosks use keys from this page, remove it from .env.docker.
kiosks.note: Only a hash of the key is stored, never the key itself. Creation and revocation are written to the audit log, and a Telegram message is sent for each new key.
